saints.name: Our Lady of the Rosary
saints.title: Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: A memorial giving thanks for the Rosary and for the deliverance of Christendom at Lepanto…
biography: This memorial honours the Blessed Virgin under the title of the Rosary, the prayer that ponders the mysteries of Christ's life, death, and glory upon the beads. It was born of battle: after the Holy League's fleet defeated the Ottoman navy at Lepanto on 7 October 1571, Pius V, who had asked all Christendom to pray the Rosary for the outcome, instituted an annual feast of Our Lady of Victory.

Two years later, in 1573, Gregory XIII renamed it the feast of the Holy Rosary and kept it on the first Sunday of October. Clement XI extended it to the whole Church in 1716 after Prince Eugene of Savoy's victory over the Turks at Peterwardein, and Pius X in 1913 fixed it again on 7 October, the anniversary of the battle.

Leo XIII, the Rosary's great champion, added 'Queen of the Most Holy Rosary' to the Litany of Loreto in 1883. The memorial thus weds a devotion long preached by the sons of St. Dominic to the Church's confidence in the intercession of the Mother of God — a garland of roses, as the name rosarium suggests, laid upon the mysteries of her Son.
saints.knownFor: The Rosary and the deliverance at Lepanto.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Feast of the Holy Rosary”
